investigation.title: local-agent-runtime Eval Failure: Upstream Model Provider Returned 424 provider_account_unavailable
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency error with error code provider_account_unavailable. The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the configured model provider at the time of the eval run, so the runtime test never completed and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The immediate root cause is a transient upstream model provider availability failure surfaced as a 424 Failed Dependency response from the AURA LLM gateway, which the harness translated into a 502 bad_gateway. Because the provider call failed before any response metadata was returned, the eval runner could not populate any of the five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) mandated by the expected-output contract in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 102–105). This is an eval infrastructure failure against a temporarily degraded external dependency, not a confirmed user-facing product outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.local-agent-create: passed with evidence keys agentId, environment, machineType, orgId — agent creation and org resolution were healthy at the same time the runtime call failed, isolating the failure to the LLM provider call path.
sibling.local-agent-permissions: passed with full permissions evidence — the permissions subsystem was unaffected, further isolating the failure to the model provider invocation step.
possibleCauses: Primary: Transient model provider outage or rate-limit event at the time of the eval run (2026-10-08T18:56:51Z), causing the AURA LLM gateway to return 424 provider_account_unavailable. The error message explicitly states this is a server-side issue unrelated to account credentials.

Secondary: A misconfigured or expired provider credential or routing rule on the AURA backend that causes provider_account_unavailable to be returned persistently rather than transiently — would require a re-run to distinguish from a transient event.

Tertiary: The eval runner's agent creation step (createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs line 1777) succeeded but the subsequent runtime/test call targeted a provider endpoint that was unavailable only for the model type assigned to local agents at that moment.

Lower probability: A regression introduced by a recent change to infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (most recent commit: 099a711) that altered how the runtime test request is constructed — however, the error message originates from the upstream provider layer, not from a malformed request, and sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty, so this is speculative.

investigation.title: Project Agent Chat Stream Eval Failure: Model Provider Returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, Blocking Session Persistence and All Downstream Checks
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-chat-stream failed at 2026-10-08T18:57:10Z because the AURA backend returned HTTP 424 with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing the chat stream to terminate with an error frame before any text was generated, a session was persisted, or the expected phrase was returned. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a backend model-provider connectivity fault; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA backend was unable to reach the upstream model provider at the time of the eval run (support_id=2c4e2170752b). The 424 Failed Dependency response was returned before the agent stream could emit a text_delta frame, produce a textSample, persist a session, or record sessionId, sessionCount, or expectedPhrase. Because the stream terminated on an error frame, all three missing required evidence fields (sessionId, sessionCount, expectedPhrase) were never written, causing the contract validation to fail. The same provider-unavailability error independently caused session-share-public-read to fail (support_id=816177d51c9a). The remaining siblings (project-agent-tool-roundtrip, project-agent-a2a-roundtrip, project-agent-subagent-roundtrip) show the same early-termination frame pattern (progress, session_ready, assistant_message_start, error, message) and zero tool invocations, consistent with the model provider being unreachable for all agent turns in this run window.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=8184, well below warningLatencyMs=30000, confirming the run terminated fast on an error rather than timing out.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Transient model provider outage or connectivity fault on the AURA backend side at the time of the eval run (~18:57–19:00 UTC on 2026-10-08). The error message explicitly states 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits.' Two distinct support_ids (2c4e2170752b, 816177d51c9a) were issued for two separate checks within the same run window, consistent with a backend-side provider routing or availability problem affecting all agent chat turns.

SECONDARY — Eval-account-level model provider quota or rate-limit exhaustion on the backend, causing all agent stream requests in this run to be rejected with 424. This would produce the same symptom but would be scoped to the eval service account rather than all users.

TERTIARY — A backend configuration or routing change that caused the model provider endpoint to become unreachable for the desktop-release runtime environment specifically. No suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis; it remains speculative.
